extracted.intended_audience: ICLR 2025 reviewers (program committee reviewers / paper reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers serving on ICLR 2025: how to read submissions, structure reviews, engage in discussion, follow ethics, and make accept/reject recommendations for conference papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and substantive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Your reviews are timely and substantive. Write a constructive, thorough and timely review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top reviewers will be acknowledged; follow the review schedule (create/update profile, bid, write review by deadlines). Timeliness includes participating in discussion and updating recommendations after discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to the ICLR Code of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviewers are required to read the Code of Ethics and adhere to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should raise potential CoE violations as part of the review process. Authors may include a CoE discussion section (not counted against page limit). If you see possible violations, complete the CoE report when submitting your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Large Language Models (LLMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of LLMs is allowed as a general-purpose assist tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reviewers remain fully responsible for content written under their name, including content generated by LLMs that could be construed as plagiarism or fabrication. LLMs are not eligible for authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the paper thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully read through the entire paper and look up related work and citations that will help you comprehensively evaluate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give yourself sufficient time. Consider the paper's objective, strong points, and weak points while reading. Supplementary material can often answer questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the objective of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the goal of the paper: address a known application/problem, draw attention to a new application/problem, introduce/explain a theoretical finding, or a combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different objectives require different considerations about potential value and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify strong points
rubrics_metrics.description: Note where the submission is clear, technically correct, experimentally rigorous, reproducible, and presents novel findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as comprehensive as possible in listing strengths; use these to justify positive recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify weak points
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify weaknesses in clarity, correctness, experimental rigor, reproducibility, novelty, or other aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be comprehensive and specific about weaknesses so authors and area chairs can act on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of potential biases; stay open-minded
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful of potential biases and try to be open-minded about the value and interest a paper can hold for the entire ICLR community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A paper may be valuable to the community even if it is not interesting to you personally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer four key questions to form recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: For recommendation, answer: (1) What specific question/problem is tackled? (2) Is the approach well motivated and well-placed in the literature? (3) Does the paper support the claims (results correct and scientifically rigorous)? (4) What is the significance of the work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four questions summarize whether a submission brings sufficient value and contributes new knowledge; significance does not necessarily require state-of-the-art results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize the paper's claimed contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize what the paper claims to contribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be positive and constructive in the summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: List strong and weak points in the review
rubrics_metrics.description: List strong and weak points of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as comprehensive as possible; separate factual/technical weaknesses from subjective opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: State a clear initial recommendation with reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state your initial recommendation (accept or reject) with one or two key reasons for this choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the core reasons explicit so ACs and authors can understand your decision basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supporting arguments for your recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide supporting arguments that justify your accept/reject recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include evidence from the paper (theory, experiments, clarity) and explain how they map to your decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask targeted questions for the authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask questions you would like answered by the authors to clarify your understanding and obtain additional evidence needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions should be constructive and aimed at addressing gaps that affect your confidence in the assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide additional feedback aimed to improve the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide additional feedback with the aim to improve the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it clear these points are to help and not necessarily part of the decision assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete the CoE report when submitting reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting your review, complete a CoE report: whether there is a potential CoE violation and, if so, explain why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the CoE before reviewing so you can answer these questions accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage actively in the discussion phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in asynchronous discussions with authors and other reviewers; authors can revise submissions during this phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open to changing your initial recommendation in light of new information; maintain constructive tone and follow up on questions you posed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participate in borderline paper meetings when requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Area Chairs will (virtually) meet with reviewers only for borderline cases; reviewers should attend if asked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with other reviewers' feedback prior to the meeting. Information may be leveraged for reviewers who fail to attend (excluding emergencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a final recommendation after discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Update your review after discussion and any author revisions, and provide a final recommendation to the area chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State your reasoning and what did/didn't change your recommendation throughout the discussion phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use supplementary material judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material is not necessary to read but can often answer questions from the main paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider reading the supplement before asking authors for clarifications that may already be answered there.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to handle policy and other violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag CoE violations via the CoE report; for other violations (plagiarism, double submission, length, formatting) contact the AC/SAC or PC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can send a confidential comment with appropriate readership restrictions to raise these issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting additional experiments: limited scope
rubrics_metrics.description: You are allowed to ask for additional experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New experiments should not significantly change the content of the submission; they should be limited in scope and serve to more thoroughly validate existing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of state-of-the-art results is not alone a rejection reason
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission not achieving state-of-the-art results does not by itself constitute grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions bring value when they convincingly demonstrate new, relevant, impactful knowledge (empirical, theoretical, practical), even without SOTA performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations about citing recent work / contemporaneous papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers published within the last four months relative to the full paper deadline are considered contemporaneous; authors are not required to compare to peer-reviewed work published within that window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to cite and discuss relevant papers, but may be excused for not knowing about very recent work or arXiv-only papers. Reviewers should use judgement and consult ACs if in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and correctness of theoretical claims and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Theoretical results should be clearly stated with correct proofs and explicit assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that theorems are novel or properly attributed, assumptions about function classes are explicit, and proof steps are verifiable; ask for clarifications where steps are unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and relation to prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper should clearly state what is novel and how it relates to prior literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If novelty is unclear, request clarifications and comparisons to closely related theorems or algorithms; do not accept unsupported novelty claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: State assumptions and scope precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state assumptions (e.g., about function classes, linear vs nonlinear settings) and the regime where results apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assumptions are implicit or inconsistent across sections, request explicit statements and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental methodology requires sufficient details
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments must include sufficient details (policy used, feature choices, architectures, parameter tuning, initialization, number of runs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing experimental details hinder reproducibility; ask for specifics on hyperparameters, training protocols, and any deviations from standard baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance and number of runs
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported results should be statistically meaningful; include appropriate numbers of runs and uncertainty estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If differences are small or number of runs is low, request more runs, error bars, or tests of significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate baselines and fair comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparisons to baselines must be fair (proper tuning, comparable architectures, and protocols).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If baselines are under-tuned or comparisons are unfair, request re-evaluation or justification of chosen settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ablation and sensitivity analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should analyze how key parameters and design choices affect results (e.g., vary k, regularization, computational cost).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request empirical studies showing tradeoffs, cost/benefit analyses, and robustness to hyperparameters where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and precision in writing, notation and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper should be precise in language, equations, and notation; avoid imprecise statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out unclear phrases, incorrect equations, inconsistent notation, and suggest concrete edits to improve clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide minor comments and suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: List minor comments that improve the manuscript but do not change the score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include typographical fixes, ordering suggestions, or requests for small clarifications in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive and respectful review tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be constructive, helpful, and respectful in tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources recommended: 'Criticising with Kindness' and other reviewer guides; phrase critiques to help authors improve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer procedural responsibilities and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete administrative tasks: create/update OpenReview profile, bid on papers, meet review and discussion deadlines, flag CoE concerns by the stated dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main tasks and dates are listed (profile update, bidding window, review submission, discussion window, CoE flagging, final recommendations). Follow them closely to support the program.
